chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: First Hollywood recording date, March 1939
summary: A tape from a Chicago friend; the last session on which Claude worked with her, with Hollywood musicians.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I should just explain that we've just been interrupted temporarily, and we're now moving over to your first recording date out in Hollywood in March, 1939.
Again, I couldn't locate many of these at the (Institute of Jazz Studies), but you have them on a tape that you have.
Do you want to say the name of the person who sent you that tape, maybe?
I have a friend out in Chicago who, a

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.
WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
couple of years ago, sent me a tape of the selections that he had in his collection.
And, of course, some of these things I had lost years ago, and even lost track of -- forgot that I had made them. And it was very good to have them so I could recollect.

And this particular group of songs that were made out of Hollywood -- this is after we made the picture. And it's got 'I Dream of Jeannie With The Light Brown Hair', 'I'm Happy About The Whole Thing', 'Drink To Me Only With Thine Eyes', and 'Corn Pickin'.'
Incidentally, this was the last time and I that Claude Thornhill/had worked together. We were going through some managerial problems at the time.
I really don't know how Claude happened to be out there unless he came out there to sort of look after his interests.
As I said before, when I first went out to California to make the picture -- when I opened at the club -- by this time, Gladys Mosier who had be instrumental in introducing me to Claude --
